HG-Quick-start-do-this-first-19: Prior to your first session, read through the induction and the full return in waking life, so you’re more familiar with them. Give yourself a chunk of time when you can be physically secure for the time it takes. Then put the screen aside; the practice is something you learn to conduct, not a checklist to keep reading.
HG-Protecting-Yourself-from-Hyp-31: Even when not actively engaging the conscious mind, there are many ways to influence people. Marketers and interface designers know this perfectly well. In the Federal Trade Commission’s report on “dark patterns,” they describe designs that trick or manipulate consumers. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) describes commercial patterns that steer, deceive, coerce, or manipulate people toward choices that may work against their interests.
HG-Keep-the-Adult-Part-of-Yours-41:
Keep the Adult Part of Yourself in Charge

Under no circumstances allow a strong state, charismatic individual, sexual charge, spiritual claim, or other authority to replace the adult part of yourself. All legitimate forms of influence can stand up to questions, sleep, boundaries and time.
HG-Forget-the-left-brain-right-61:
The mind of love and the mind of analysis can BOTH be there - warmth and brightness. The mind of intuition and the mind of rationality can BOTH be there - intuitive signals without dogma, and testing of those signals without killing them. The body can have a voice - saying yes or no or not yet. The imagination can have opened up the field and then the adult can choose what to do next in the real world…. It can be peaceful but also precise.

Without the mind of love the mind of analysis can be sterile. Without the mind of analysis the mind of love can lead to fantasy. Without testing intuitive signals they can become delusions. Without intuitive signals the testing can be dead. So these modes can correct each other.

And it’s got to lead somewhere: kinder behavior, more humility, better judgment, real service, or a more workable ordinary life.
HG-Why-doing-it-myself-worked-b-65:
Doing self-hypnosis on my own seems far more useful than the very little I managed to do with a professional hypnotist. I was sober at the session and didn't feel especially suggestible, but I suspect that's not even the main reason the pro didn't work very well for me. The bigger issue was trust and precision.

When I do it on my own, I can detect when the wording I'm using for a suggestion to my subconscious is slightly off, and talk to my subconscious to find out what it thinks is wrong with the wording. When I use an image, I can tell whether it's giving me useful information, or just telling me what I'm afraid of, or what I want to avoid, or what I want to be true, or something I don't understand yet. And I can notice my body saying no before my conscious mind talks me into a yes.
HG-Why-doing-it-myself-worked-b-68: Self-hypnosis simply has one advantage nobody outside can duplicate: immediate dialogue with the system itself. I found that especially amplified with loveyhuasca. My experiences included a much deeper understanding of my motivations, peaceful loving awareness operating alongside analytical clarity, the disappearance of unhelpful daydreaming, different priorities around relationships, stronger intuition, and repeated correction between intuition, subconscious response, and conscious analysis.
HG-The-inner-child-the-guards-a-92:
Here I’m going to talk about what you develop in yourself as you reparent your inner child. I’m going to talk about it in terms of three jobs: your loving Nurturer, your safe Adult Protector (hereafter just the Protector) and your wise Guide. That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, and each job keeps the others in balance. It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.

Also, your inner child’s worth is not dependent on these qualities… It has its own worth, and its own qualities, like playing, being tender, not taking life too seriously, being creative and wondering at the world. Those belong in your relationship with it too, not just the wounds.
HG-When-the-adult-role-is-not-a-96:
For that starting point, I have developed a kind of provisional bridge that I call “borrowed adulthood.” It’s built from familiar practices like modeling and supported action, but I’m not suggesting that the whole sequence has been formally tested and proven as one treatment.

Access your witnessing position if necessary, just noticing what’s there, without needing it to be warm or wise or certain. If you already know how to access different internal positions, move immediately to accessing the adult position you want to borrow.
HG-Love-doesn-t-have-to-wait-fo-110: You could say something like, "Okay. I believe that you don't believe me. I still love you. You don't have to love me back. Tell me what feels unsafe." Try not to turn "I still love you" into a line you say on cue, though, because then it can brush the anger off, and what it's really saying is "so stop being angry."
HG-Working-with-your-guards-139:
Instead, you might feel numb, cynical, angry, hungry, like you need to look at your phone, sexually aroused, like you need to make plans, sleepy, dissociated, or you might even think that what you're doing is stupid. Those are not failures. Often what you're experiencing is a very charming guard. It's what protects you when your consciously installed parental Protector isn't functioning, the same as when you were a child. But before you decide where it's coming from, ask it what it's trying to stop, or what it wants. It could also be your inner child, mad that you took so long to come back, or your inherited parent script, or something from earlier today, or a bit of each.

(To the guard, in the same Nurturer voice you meant for your inner child: “I see you. I'm not going to force my way past you. What's going on?” Then wait and listen patiently. If nothing comes, that's fine for now. At some point you can ask, “What are you afraid would happen if you stopped protecting me by…..?”)
HG-What-an-induction-is-actuall-234: Getting yourself ready to do something. Part of that is gathering your attention up. Part of that might be deepening. Part of that is letting what you notice inform the words you're hearing and what you do next. There are lots of different ways to do this. For this method, I'm going to be counting, but you could do all sorts of things. If you want to just talk, or tell a story, or move, or make sounds, or be curious, or whatever, by all means, just do that. The only thing is, say that you're doing it. Don't pretend you're doing something else, in the name of elegance or whatever.
HG-Please-don-t-put-six-metapho-237:
Keep it simple. One thing you're doing, one anchor/image you're going with at first, one way of coming back, and feel free to set a tone (warm, bounded, directed, neutral witnessing, whatever) for yourself. If you're going to use metaphors just do one, and if you switch metaphors, do it in a way that's conscious.

Using metaphors and imagery is entirely optional. You can use whatever form of signal shows up (feelings, rhythms, movements, words, spatial sense, simple knowing, lack of signal, whatever) but if you're using words, try to keep them related to whatever world you're creating. If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world. And when you're done, come back the other way. (You can borrow qualities such as warmth or steadiness, but don't change who you are.)

When you're writing the script, decide what the verb you're using is, what the sensory quality is, what the short refrain is, and how you're going to transition between ideas. Read it out loud as you're writing it. Long, elegant sentences don't read well when you're being induced. It's all just soup.
HG-Before-you-begin-241:
Read this page, and the Come all the way back page, when you're awake.

Get clear on what it is you want to do during the induction. What do you want not to do today? How long do you want to spend on this? (You don't have to do this on a problem. You can do it on something you want to experience more of: love, play, confidence, creativity, communion, whatever.) Make sure you're leaving some time at the end to come back, and reflect on what you experienced.
HG-Before-you-begin-244:
Deciding to do it: how will you coax yourself to do this? Make it spacious? Make it warm and held? Make it firmer, so you stay with a feeling? Something else? Preview what you are going to do: will you close your eyes? Will you come out and go back in again? What will you do at the end? If you are going to use a recording, read the script beforehand if you can. Know that you can say "stop" at any time and the induction will end. If you want to change something, say "less" if you want it to be asking for less from you, or say "quiet" and the talking will stop. You can also just open your eyes and stop, and then come all the way back anyway. You don't need to ask any parts for permission to stop, even if a part tells you that you do.

If you are new to this or haven't done it for a while, work on the coming in and coming out part first, don't bring in the hard stuff till later. You don't have to watch yourself all the time, but for the first few times, make sure you can change state. Let yourself make it easier and easier to do this and notice that it takes less and less of you to do it. A no will stay a no. The narrator can't add stuff just because you don't say anything.

Let your response guide you as to what to do next regardless of what the script is expecting. Utilize: use what you have (a thought, sound, movement, or objection) to go to the next place, whatever it is. Learn how to notice what is there. Learn how to notice if there is no change, and that no change is not a secret success. For more on language you can use, see Appendix B, or keep reading below for information on using the tools after induction in Let the next response guide you. Either way, keep the instructions about how to stay safe and how to get out plain.
HG-Sober-induction-3-5-minutes-259:
Let your attention come back to your chosen anchor. 4. Let more of your attention come to what you've found. 3. Leave a little space. 2. See if you can listen to a space after the words without preparing an answer. 1. Take your time.

Bring to mind, if you want, the thing that you want to talk about, or just the wish to have inner contact. Just let it be there for now. You don't need to tell the whole story yet.

What do you notice now?
HG-Already-open-Contain-before-267:
Orient yourself by looking around. Where are you? What's the date or day? How does your body feel? Where are you grounded? Can you feel your feet/hands/spine/etc? Make some contact with yourself, eg press your thumbs against the tips of your index fingers gently but firmly so that you can feel friction. Focus on that.

Say something like, "Only what I can integrate, please. If there's too much it can wait. My body may stay safe. I'll be here as an adult, this won't just be my inner child."
HG-Make-the-hypnosis-more-activ-276:
If being still tends to make you sleepy, or diffuse your attention, or make you want to mentally escape, you can make the hypnosis more active. Instead of getting more relaxed with the hypnosis, try getting more alert. Keep your eyes open. Pair a small repeated hand movement with increasing clarity; stop the movement and notice what remains. Don't escape inside yourself. Say something like,

“Starting with your eyes open press your thumb to your forefinger. And as you press your fingers together gently and release, you begin to bring yourself into a place of clearer awareness… again you press your fingers together and release, bringing yourself into an even clearer state of awareness. And again as you press your fingers together and release you bring yourself into a clear state of awareness, and now you stop pressing your fingers together and in the first second after you stop pressing your fingers together deliberately, you can notice if there is any echo of the pressing in your fingers, in your breathing, in your attention or nowhere at all. Just notice, keep yourself up straight and work at this level.
HG-The-two-hand-induction-281:
Start to breathe gently….

“Love above, Child below, Adult present”

“Sending my love down to my Child. If something comes back up, I let it, and send my love on down again. If nothing comes back, I just keep sending mine, and listening.”
HG-Sleep-induction-285:
Sleep induction is different than inner work, where you need to come back up to write things down and do actions.

You can tell your analytical mind to stand down, any revelations can wait.

Check out Nimja’s sleep playlist to go to sleep listening to hypnosis
HG-Optional-fractionation-pract-289: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. At some point in time you can add this, but you must say you are doing it before doing it, so no answer can secretly mean “deeper.”
HG-Capacity-before-content-377:
“Dear Wise Subconscious Mind, if there is something you know that my conscious self is not ready to know, please don’t break it open violently! Do what you can to make me able to know it in a way that is safe! Prepare me BEFORE you break it open! Ground me BEFORE you show me the memory! Support me BEFORE you make it intense! Give me one next action!” etc.

REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it relates to trauma and memory. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!
HG-Nothing-happens-378:
REMEMBER: Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal, especially if it relates to trauma and memory. The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc. So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!

Troubleshooting

Nothing happens

Is there a way you could try this on a smaller scale?

Ask: “Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”
HG-It-feels-fake-384: Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake? The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc. It doesn't matter that you don't have an inner voice/image to do this, it isn't necessarily about not having a 'grown up' or resisting doing the work. If it feels like you are being asked to do something you don't want to do then correct the invitation. It could be that there is a part that is protecting you, so talk to it.
HG-Core-prompts-480:
Once you get an answer, you can ask: “What can I do in my ordinary life to prove that I heard correctly?” If it tells you to do something, I'd only do it if it's loving and leaves you free. It should make sense, too. Even then, anything big or hard to undo can wait until you're calm and you've checked it against what you actually know.

The prompt will tell your subconscious what you want. The NLP in Appendix B can help you get it in a safer way, but that doesn’t make the answer automatically true.
HG-Pattern-5-Embedded-invitatio-509:
An embedded invitation places a small direction inside a larger sentence. It should invite a modest inner movement, not hide a demand. ie. "And I can allow myself to experience..."

or, "As I sit here, I may begin to allow myself to become aware..."
HG-Pattern-6-Ethical-double-bin-514:
Manipulative Double Bind Questions are set up so that whatever you answer, you end up doing what the speaker wants.

An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes. Ethical Double Bind Questions might be:

"Would you prefer to allow a feeling of warmth to come over you now, or would you prefer a feeling of space?"
HG-Reframing-changing-the-meani-561: Reframes are dishonest when they make the problem into something that was good all along. Instead ask yourself: What else might be true? or What is this part trying to do for me? or How might my Nurturer reframe this? or How might my Protector reframe this? or How might my Guide reframe this? etc., etc.
HG-Perceptual-positions-self-ot-564: Perceptual Positions: 1) seeing from Self (what do I feel from inside myself?), 2) then seeing from Other (if I sit inside the other person, what might they be feeling or protecting?), 3) then seeing from Witness (if I watched this from across the room, what would I notice?), and 4) then seeing from Universal Heart (what serves truth, love, boundaries, and the good of everyone involved?). I do this to see the situation with more accuracy.
HG-What-I-will-not-use-NLP-for-574:
Here is a list of things I do not do with NLP, to myself or to others:

I do not use NLP to talk myself out of a real signal.

I do not tell people to override their fear before asking what it’s protecting.

I do not use NLP for memory retrieval.

I do not use NLP to manipulate other people or convince myself an intuition is true.

I do not remove pain, hunger, grief, anger, or medical symptoms.
HG-Appendix-D-Anxiety-body-firs-616: Remember that often the anxiety comes from a childhood guard part of you. It’s what protects you when your inner adult’s Protector isn’t functioning, the same as in childhood. It’s trying to help, making a guess about what’s coming: that you are in danger, or may be shamed, or abandoned, or fail, or be exposed, or be sick, or be rejected, or lose control, or feel something it believes would be unbearable. It can be right! It’s probably been wrong before too, and you know some of those times. Therefore, instead of interrogating that part, start with yourself:
HG-Body-supports-627:
Work with the body. Sometimes the mind is too activated for meditation to help, so you may need to work directly with the body to calm it down. Maybe get a massage, or massage a foot, your scalp, a temple, or the back of the neck, the top of a shoulder, etc. (Avoid massaging the front of the neck. Also avoid massaging injured or numb body parts, or bruised, inflamed, or recently surgically operated on areas, or varicose veins. Also stop if the massage makes the anxiety symptoms worse, or makes you feel bad in any way, such as painful, dizzy, tingly, etc.) There are many other somatic approaches you can try, like heat, pressure, a weighted blanket, darkness, your favorite calming music, a careful use of a massage gun, etc. Use the support that actually helps, rather than assembling a tiny wellness trade show around the anxiety.

I have a page on my ZHoly3O product, which is ozonated charcoal, and I talk about this “holy water” as one of the things that can help you relax. (See the mention of Blushield on that page, too.) But neither one of those products is necessary. All you really need is to stabilize yourself, and then listen to the messages from your inner realm, reality test those messages, and then take one grounded action.
HG-Inner-child-love-630: Here is some inner child love. Put your hand over your heart and your other hand on your solar plexus, and say to yourself in a loving way, “Little one, you are not alone. You don’t have to fix it. I’m here now, and the adult is here now to listen to you.” Make sure you are actually talking to your inner child, who is scared to death. No warmth today? Then rest your hands there and notice what you find, no faking required.
HG-Appendix-F-Self-trust-outsid-647: That said, self hypnosis may be the best way of talking to your subconscious on a day to day basis. If you’re dealing with particularly complicated trauma, blind spots, dissociation, destabilization, or relational wounds that need another nervous system, skilled outside support may be best.
HG-Forgiveness-without-bypass-675:
A helpful understanding to come to is that while their actions were harmful, in a sense, they could only make the moves they made, given their accumulated nature at the time (conditioning, history, pain, capacity, etc). This doesn’t negate that harm was caused, and it doesn’t stop you from holding someone accountable, allowing for consequences, working on making different moves now, etc. It simply helps us come to a place where we aren’t expecting something from someone that they can’t give. It doesn’t make their limitations matter any less.

“You don’t have to forgive before you’re ready. I won’t use spirituality to silence your pain. And I won’t build our whole life around this wound forever.”
HG-Forgiveness-without-bypass-678: What actually happened? What was the impact? What boundaries need to be set? What shaped the other person(s) into someone capable of that harm? What is theirs? What is mine? What does accountability require? How can I let this go, without denying any of the above?
HG-Forgiving-yourself-680: For self-forgiveness, name what you did, but don't take responsibility for what wasn't yours. Let yourself feel the remorse and take in the harm, or how it went against your values, and stop short of making yourself a permanent criminal.
HG-Appendix-G-Altered-states-683: This is NOT to say that you SHOULD use substances, but many people have used them when they first did self-hypnosis, contacted their inner child, or talked to their Higher Self. I’d learn the inner child work sober first, with enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep (see the inner child reparenting section). Borrowing them is fine, as long as it’s from someone steady who won’t try to run your trip for you.
HG-Appendix-G-Altered-states-685: A lot of people have OPENED themselves up to love at one point in their life. If you've had a similar experience, know that there is a difference between having experienced it at one point, or only being able to access it in a certain state, and being able to get to it at any point in your life. Let that experience show you what's possible, while you build a way to get to it in everyday life. (If you can't give that love to the child, try to deal with why you can't, instead of trying to ramp up the experience. Often it’s a protective part that’s seen love come with strings before. Hear it out first.)
HG-7-Care-workshop-751: Care workshop: prepare the workshop (time, place, tools, boundaries, etc). Invite the signal/feeling/young part to come only as close as is welcome. Try to avoid any language that makes you feel you're not one person. Care for it as best you can, by asking what it wants and giving that if you can, or sensing into it and responding, or just being with it. Take breaks, get back in contact if that's ok, take more breaks, etc. Keep bringing in adult functions (or borrow someone else's function). Have the adult part of you run the show. Goal is to make it "good as you" rather than "good as new", not to erase history. Tell your little one, "That's enough for today. We're going back to the life we're building." Close the workspace, reassure yourself that you are one whole person, that you're an adult now, and come back.
HG-8-Resource-embodiment-753: Resource: pick a resource quality you understand (warmth, boundary, steadiness, curiosity, or dignity). Imagine yourself accessing 1% more of that quality (or, if you prefer, just observe it rather than embody it). What is different? How is your body, voice, etc? Do this a few times to strengthen it. Come back, keeping the quality and one positive action that you would do with it, but leaving the imagined you behind, saying "I am me".
HG-9-No-trance-inner-contact-755: For the no trance inner contact, I would do: Pacing: notice you can see, it's (day of the week), you have feet, you can read, you can write, etc. Suggestion: in your mind, ask one clear question and wait, but don't focus too hard. Choice: you can answer the question, write an answer, write that you don't know, take a break, rephrase the question, ask someone else, stop doing this, etc. Autonomous signal: write whatever you get (a word, sensation, impulse, objection, or silence) without interpreting it as proof. Deepener: none (full alertness isn't a lesser version). Handoff: have your adult self answer the question in whatever way is appropriate, preferably by writing or doing. Integration/exit: reality test the signal and do one small thing based on it. Since you didn't go into trance, just close the exercise and carry on with your day.
HG-Appendix-K-Sources-and-furth-757: The personal accounts and the way I arrange this practice are my own, especially adaptations like the one I'm doing here where I am combining body-oriented work and hypnotic work. This combination is not a validated form of treatment at this time.
